title: [review] project-LICHEN-worker6-tkjl: from_bytes returns packed wire data as payload, skipping decode
description:
## Bug: from_bytes does not unpack wire-encoded payload

**File:** `rust/lichen-schc/src/fragment.rs:171-199`

**Severity:** P0 — data corruption

The `Fragment::from_bytes` method returns wire-packed data as the Fragment payload:

```rust
// Regular fragment: payload borrows raw wire bytes from position 2
payload: rest,  // &data[2..] — still in packed 7-bit format

// All-1 fragment: payload borrows raw wire bytes after MIC  
payload: &rest[MIC_LENGTH..],  // still in packed format
```

The wire format packs each 8-bit byte as: `out[n+2] = byte << 1`, with bit 7 of each byte ORed into `out[n+1]`. `from_bytes` must reverse this encoding before returning the fragment.

**Impact:** When a FragmentReceiver receives fragments parsed from wire, `copy_from_slice(fragment.payload)` stores packed data into the reassembly buffer. Fragments created by FragmentSender have original bytes — the receiver cannot distinguish between the two, leading to mixed packed/unpacked data in the final packet.

**Evidence:** The shared test vector `recover_missing_regular_tile` expects wire format `0x787c` (header) + zeros, but our `write_to` produces `0x783e` — the FCN field is not shifted left by 1 to match the test vector wire encoding scheme where bit 0 of the header carries the first payload byte top bit.

Related: header bit layout (window at bit 7, FCN at bits 6-1) also needs to match test vectors.
